lenses_summary.verification_red_team: C1 confirmed by Reuters via BNN Bloomberg plus Creative Bloq and designcompass. Do not claim the name 'failed' or that customers rejected it: reaction is social posts and one analyst view ('ego-driven'). Deal value ($110bn) and Oct 6 legal name change are reported, not audited. Do not say how the logo was designed beyond what designcompass states. C3 replacement status unknown; C5 Zappi number secondary only; C8 vendor data.
lenses_summary.audience_psychology: Every business owner has felt the urge to put their own name on the door. The tension 'who is the name for?' is personal (ego, family name, shareholders) and practical. Movie-studio logos are universally known images; no need for English fluency to feel it.
lenses_summary.brand_fit: Behnood = strategist/designer talking to business owners. Naming and brand architecture is core work. Regional relevance high: family holding groups and multi-brand companies across the audience's markets wrestle with parent-name vs product-name. Safe, non-political (avoid monopoly/news-politics angle, CNN/CBS editorial disputes).

gates.story_gate: C1+C11 wins: central tension (the merger's name honours neither famous studio; the name on the building vs the name on the screen) and a concrete image (the studio logo before a film; a brass nameplate on a door vs a cinema ticket). C5 has a strong number but repeats the pricing theme of 2026-10-25; C3 repeats 2026-10-26.
gates.repeat_check: 2026-10-30 dealt with visual consistency inside one brand's packaging; tomorrow is about naming and who a name serves (parent vs product). Different question, different imagery.

decision.why: Fresh, verified spark; evergreen idea underneath usable by any business owner with more than one product; works equally for Persian and international audiences.
